headline: Revenue and EBITDA climb, attributable loss widens
summary_short: Clearway's Q1 FY2026 revenue rose to $354M (+18.8% y/y, +14.2% q/q) and Adjusted EBITDA reached $257M, but the loss attributable to Clearway Energy widened to -$163M (diluted EPS -$1.35) from -$3M a year ago, even as the company's consolidated net loss narrowed to $68M from $104M.
summary_long: Revenue grew 18.8% y/y and 14.2% q/q to $354M, helped by 8% higher Renewables & Storage generation from growth investments. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $257M (+2% y/y) on growth-investment contributions, partly offset by lower wind resource. Consolidated Net Loss narrowed to $68M from $104M on smaller mark-to-market hedge losses, but loss attributable to Clearway Energy, Inc. widened to $163M from $3M because noncontrolling-interest allocation swung from a $101M loss to a $95M gain. Operating cash flow jumped to $401M from $95M, driven largely by $282M of transferable tax-credit proceeds. Cash rose to $325M; long-term debt grew to $8,504M after the Cardinal Portfolio acquisition and Honeycomb funding. The company reaffirmed FY2026 CAFD guidance of $470-510M and Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1,441-1,481M.

drivers.explanation: Renewables & Storage generation was 8% higher y/y, primarily due to the contribution of growth investments.
Adjusted EBITDA increase driven by contribution from growth investments, partially offset by lower wind resource at certain facilities.
Consolidated Net Loss actually narrowed on smaller mark-to-market hedge losses, but attributable loss widened because noncontrolling-interest allocation flipped from a $101M loss to a $95M gain.
Increase is largely explained by $282M of proceeds from transferable tax credits recognized this quarter versus none in Q1 2025, per the cash-flow statement.
Company reaffirmed 2026 financial guidance, cited an accelerating 12.7 GW late-stage growth pipeline, on-time Cardinal Portfolio close, and stockholder approval of share-class simplification.
